Reverse engineering

Firmware Extraction and Analysis

Planned notes on extracting firmware, identifying embedded filesystems, and examining binaries, configuration files, exposed services, and stored credentials.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series will examine firmware extraction and filesystem analysis with binwalk, followed by inspection of binaries and configuration in embedded Linux images. Topics include hardcoded credentials, command injection, and exposed services.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Target selection and legal scope

  • Choose a device from the owned lab inventory and record its provenance.
  • Define what may be extracted, retained, and published.
  • Record board revision, firmware version, and access method.

Image acquisition

  • Read external flash or eMMC with an in-circuit or desoldered setup.
  • Capture vendor update files and compare them with the on-device image.
  • Hash every dump and keep the original read-only.

Filesystem and signature triage

  • Use entropy and signature scans to locate containers and compressed regions.
  • Extract embedded filesystems and document offsets and tool versions.
  • Identify the bootloader, kernel, and application layout.

Configuration and binary review

  • Inspect init scripts, service definitions, and configuration files.
  • Look for hardcoded credentials, keys, and debug interfaces.
  • Trace exposed services and command paths into binaries.

Findings and disclosure

  • Record each observation with its supporting artifact.
  • Assess impact and remediation options.
  • Follow coordinated disclosure before publishing sensitive details.

Topics to cover

  • Firmware extraction
  • binwalk and embedded filesystems
  • Hardcoded credentials
  • Command injection
  • Exposed services
